### Summary

The premise and hypothesis in this example are genuinely semantically contradictory (the premise says the program "will help improve" lawyers' public image; the hypothesis says it "isn't going to improve" it). However, **~14 of the 20 active features are negation-word detectors** rather than features that encode the relational contradiction between the two sentences. These features could equally fire on non-contradiction cases involving negation (e.g., two negated entailing statements like "It didn't help" / "It wasn't useful"), indicating they encode a surface-level negation heuristic rather than genuine semantic contradiction modeling. The model's correct prediction here is therefore likely driven by these spurious negation signals rather than a true understanding of the entailment relationship.
